newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

At yesterday's annual meeting of CSR Ltd, the company warned that profits in 1998 will be achieved primarily through cost cutting. The comments followed an attack on the group by shareholders who are unhappy over the level of returns for the last five years. Page 21.

Optus Communications and rival pay-TV operator Foxtel are expected to soon reach agreement on programming arrangements. The breakthrough came as Foxtel concluded a in-principle deal to merge with Australis Media Ltd. Page 21.

A Federal Court heard yesterday that Federal Treasurer Peter Costello was advised by the Foreign Investment Review Board to consult with Canadian broadcaster CanWest Global Communications CSGs.TO before ordering it to reduce its holdings in the Ten Network. CanWest is seeking to have Costello's ruling revoked. Page 22.

Australian company Mayne Nickless Ltd has launched its second logistics joint venture in South-East Asia. Mayne Nickless said yesterday the deal involved a long-term contract with Unilever Malaysia to develop transport, warehousing, distribution and other services. Page 28.

Western Australia-based pharmaceutical group Inovax Ltd announced yesterday plans to purchase Indonesian drug group PT Ponco for about A$95 million. The move will double the company's size and allow it to diversify into manufacturing. Page 24.

Drug company Biota Holdings BIO.AX announced yesterday an extension of its agreement with CSIRO to develop oral treatments for diabetes. Biota chief executive Hugh Niall confirmed that investment in the project would be increased and said he was confident the coming year would see progress in product development. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

BHP announced yesterday it was holding talks with the Indonesian Government on the proposed A$880.9 million public float of that country's largest steel manufacturer, PT Krakatau Steel. BHP refused to confirm rumours that it plans to acquire a 25 per cent stake in Krakatau, but unnamed sources say the deal is at the 'point of finalisation'. Page 23.

Retiring CSR chairman Alan Coates has quashed speculation of a rift between the company's board and managing director Geoff Kells over CSR's recent disappointing earnings. Speaking at the annual meeting in Sydney, Coates further commented that CSR remained a major player in the cyclical commodities market, and that a significant improvement in profits was expected for the coming year. Page 23.

The A$2.2 billion global offering of ICI Australia shares is proving to be a profitable venture for retail investors, with shares increasing by 5.5 per cent at the end of trading yesterday. Parent company Imperial Chemical Industries set aside 58 million shares for retail investors when it placed a total of 143 million shares on the market. Page 24.

Anaconda Nickel has completed financing requirements for its 60 per cent stake in the A$900 million Murrin Murrin nickel project in Western Australia. Anaconda chief executive Andrew Forrest said yesterday that the company now had sufficient cash flow to proceed with stage 2 of the Murrin Murrin project and other related ventures. Page 24.

Soap and laboratory services group Campbell Brothers has announced a 62 per cent jump in first-half profit to A$5 million. Chairman Rod White told shareholders at the annual meeting yesterday that the result was due to recent acquisitions and debt reduction, and the company was considering further acquisitions worth up to A$30 million. Page 25.

The Federal Government's recent decision to liberalise dumping laws in relation to China has threatened an A$80 million chemical investment. Monsanto Australia confirmed yesterday the new policy has forced it to reassess plans to increase production at its Melbourne glyphosate and acid manufacturing plant. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

WMC quadrupled its gold forward sale program during the same period as the Reserve Bank of Australia's sale of A$2 billion in gold bullion. The move will protect WMC from damaging fallout from the recent collapse of world gold prices. Page 2.

The expected involvement by Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) in a consortium to develop the Melbourne Docklands is regarded as an attempt to secure the Australian Football League (AFL) TV rights from the Seven Network when they next become available in 2002. PBL is believed to be aiming to turn the Melbourne Docklands into a suitable stadium venue for AFL matches, with the AFL already agreeing to pay A$30 million for major tenant rights. Page 25.

According to Wattyl company secretary John Blaikie, the ACCC approval of a merger between rivals Taubmans and Bristol will result in some restructuring in the industry but is not expected to affect the company's profits. Page 27

An independent report on the proposed A$2.2 billion merger between QNI and the nickel interests of mining giant Gencor is expected to be released in ten days. The initial market reaction to the proposal saw QNI shares slide from A$2.77 to A$2.25, although the price has since partially recovered. Page 28

Up to 5,000 Australian small businesses have already registered with the Olympics Business Information Service so as to position themselves to win prestigious Olympic business in the hope that it will lead to better contracts. Page 29

ICI Australia chief executive Philip Weickhardt has criticised the Federal Government for fostering a "two-speed economy". Weickhardt says that economic growth is unsatisfactory and called for the Federal Government to promote micro-economic reform in the gas, electricity and shipping sectors. Page 25.
THE AGE

Insurance giant AMP Society has attacked criticisms of its demutualisation plan, claiming it defends the interests of its two million society members who are entitled to a stake in the A$10 billion float. AMP's chief financial officer Paul Batchelor said yesterday the company was not aiming at long-term invulnerability from takeovers and was prepared to overturn proposed anti-takeover provisions if an offer was made. Page B3.

National Australia Bank's (NAB) venture with Korean commercial bank Kookmin Bank progressed further yesterday with the securing of a New Zealand banking licence. Kookmin Bank has negotiated an agreement with NAB's subsidiary, Bank of New Zealand, to offer retail banking services for expatriate Koreans. Page B3.

Australian corporate cardholders of US credit card company American Express will be among the company's first customers to be issued with smart cards, with the first domestic trials to begin within the year. The cards will feature Proton electronic-purse technology that will offer a wider range of services to consumers. Page B3.

The half-yearly economic survey by The Age newspaper has revealed that politicians and economists are opposed on the best means to increase investment in Australia. Politicians propose increased use of industry policies to encourage sector growth, but economists oppose such active intervention and support the Department of Treasury's policy of reducing business costs. Page B3.

A report by HSBC James Capel Australia, and commissioned by Country Road, has forecast difficult times ahead for the clothing retailer. The report predicts a 61 per cent profit fall for the past year and says the company will not improve on 1995 and 1996 profit levels until 1999. Page B2.

Diversified resources company North Ltd will pay $10 million over five years for a 75 per cent stake in Coolgardie Gold's zinc/lead Gregory site in Queensland. The decision is expected to breathe new life into the project. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
